Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, task planning and other similar works in their specific field of telecommunications.
Facility for handling specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Know and apply basic elements of economics and human resource management, project organization and planning, as well as legislation, regulation and standardization in telecommunications.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of engineering projects.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in their field, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.

syllabus_topics: Quality models. ISO 9001 quality management model. Quality audits. System certification. EFQM excellence model.
Statistical process control. Basic and advanced tools. Guidelines for improvement.
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, evaluation will be continuous with group and/or individual assignments and two theory exams. The final grade must be at least 5 out of 10 to pass the course. In the extraordinary call, a theoretical-practical exam accounts for 60% of the grade, and individual/group assignments for the remaining 40%. For the extraordinary advanced call, a single theoretical-practical exam accounts for 100% of the grade. For differentiated evaluation and Erasmus students, the assessment is a theoretical-practical exam (60%) and individual/group assignments (40%).
